record.title: Jewel characterization conjecture for regularity of binomial edge ideals
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and let $J_T$ be its binomial edge ideal in $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n]$. Denote by $\#\{\text{internal vertices of }T\}$ the number of internal vertices of $T$, and let Jewel be the tree depicted in the source paper.
**Jewel characterization conjecture.** The tree $T$ contains Jewel as a subgraph if and only if

$$
\operatorname{reg}(S/J_T)\geq \#\{\text{internal vertices of }T\}+2.
$$

The forward implication follows from the observation that a tree containing Jewel has regularity at least the number of internal vertices plus two; the converse was suggested by examples computed using SAGE and Macaulay 2 and remains conjectural.
record.source_name: A. V. Jayanthan, N. Narayanan and B. V. Raghavendra Rao, “Regularity of Binomial Edge Ideals of Certain Block Graphs”, arXiv:1601.01086 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.01086

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

record.title: The eventual special-vertex conjecture for Hanoi border paths
record.statement: Let $p\geq 3$, let $G^{(p)}_{n+1}$ contain the copy $AG^{(p)}_n$, and let $S_{n_0}$ be the recursively defined border set. Let $a$ be the vertex labeled $A^{n_0+1}$, and call a vertex special when its label has the form $A^{n-i}X^i$ with $X\in{\cal A}_p\setminus\{A,B\}$ in the relevant shortest-path setting. **Eventual special-vertex conjecture.** For any $p\geq 3$, there is $n_0\geq 2$ such that for any $v\in S_{n_0}$ there is a shortest path from $a$ to $v$ that meets a special vertex. This is proposed as the inductive base needed for the partial proof of the special-vertex result; the supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: Janez Žerovnik, “Self Similarities of the Tower of Hanoi Graphs and a proof of the Frame-Stewart Conjecture”, arXiv:1601.04298 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.04298

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

record.title: Solymosi's rational expansion conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f\in\mathbb Q[x,y]$ be a polynomial of degree $d$, and let $A\subset\mathbb Q$. **Solymosi's conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
|f(A\times A)|=\Omega_d(|A|^{1+c}),
$$

unless $f(x,y)=g(ax+by)$ or $f(x,y)=g((x+a)^\alpha(y+b)^\beta)$ for $a,b\in\mathbb Q$ and positive integers $\alpha,\beta$. This is the rational-field analogue of the Elekes–Rónyai expansion problem and is open in the survey.
record.source_name: Frank de Zeeuw, “A survey of Elekes-Rónyai-type problems”, arXiv:1601.06404 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.06404

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

record.title: Georgakopoulos–Mohar conjecture on Hamilton circles in planar Cayley graphs
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely generated 3-connected planar Cayley graph. A **Hamilton circle** is a homeomorphic image of $S^1$ in the Freudenthal compactification of the graph that contains every vertex. **Georgakopoulos–Mohar conjecture.** Every finitely generated 3-connected planar Cayley graph admits a Hamilton circle. This is the broader conjecture for which the preceding three-involution problem is proposed as a first step; the source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Babak Miraftab and Tim Rühmann, “From cycles to circles in Cayley graphs”, arXiv:1708.03476 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.03476

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

record.title: Class P' conjecture for primitive morphism fixed points
record.statement:
Let ${\mathbf u}$ be a palindromic fixed point of a primitive morphism $\varphi$. A morphism is said to be of **class $P'$** if it has the class-$P'$ property used in the source. Its fixed point is required to have the same language as ${\mathbf u}$.

**Class $P'$ conjecture.** There exists a morphism of class $P'$ such that its fixed point has the same language as ${\mathbf u}$.

The conjecture is partially resolved: the binary case is solved, and affirmative answers are known for several special classes of morphisms, including marked morphisms and codings of a non-degenerate exchange of three intervals. The general case over larger alphabets remains open.
record.source_name: Edita Pelantová and Štěpán Starosta, “On Words with the Zero Palindromic Defect”, arXiv:1708.06911 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06911

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2017). “Counterexamples to the conjecture were given in .”

record.title: Star-minimization conjecture for the least $A_\alpha$-eigenvalue
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices with $\frac{1}{2}<\alpha<1$. **Star-minimization conjecture.**

$$
\lambda_n(A_{\alpha}(G))\geq\lambda_n(A_{\alpha}(K_{1,n-1})),
$$

with equality if and only if $G\cong K_{1,n-1}$. This conjecture asks whether the star minimizes the least eigenvalue of $A_\alpha$ among connected graphs of order $n$ in the specified range of $\alpha$; no resolution is stated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Huiqiu Lin, Jie Xue and Jinlong Shu, “On the A_α-spectra of graphs”, arXiv:1709.00182 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.00182

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2017). “One year later, the conjecture was confirmed by Cardoso, Cvetkovi\'{c}, Rowlinson and Simi\'c .”

record.title: The simple ordering conjecture for zero-sum subsets of abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $(G,+)$ be an abelian group. Let $A$ be a finite subset of $G\setminus\{0\}$ such that no $2$-subset $\{x,-x\}$ is contained in $A$, and suppose that

$$
\sum_{a\in A}a=0.
$$

A **simple ordering** of $A$ is an ordering of its elements whose successive partial sums are distinct. **Simple ordering conjecture.** There exists a simple ordering of the elements of $A$. This conjecture would imply that every Heffter array is simple; its validity was proposed in earlier work, while the existence of square integer Heffter arrays is known. The general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Simone Costa, Fiorenza Morini, Anita Pasotti and Marco Antonio Pellegrini, “Globally simple Heffter arrays and orthogonal cyclic cycle decompositions”, arXiv:1709.05812 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.05812

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2017).

record.title: The pure-EKR conjecture for generalized cluster complexes
record.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be a finite root system of rank $n-1$, let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal C(m,\Phi)$ denote the $m$-th generalized cluster complex, a flag pure simplicial complex of dimension $n-2$.

**Generalized cluster complex conjecture.** Every generalized cluster complex $\mathcal C(m,\Phi)$ is pure-EKR.

For type $A_{n-1}$, these complexes are the complexes of $(m+2)$-angulations of a convex $(mn+2)$-gon. The paper reports computational verification for $n+m\leq 8$ and all irreducible root systems of rank $n-1$, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Jorge Olarte, Francisco Santos, Jonathan Spreer and Christian Stump, “The EKR property for flag pure simplicial complexes without boundary”, arXiv:1710.02518 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.02518

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2017).

record.title: The Ramsey equivalence conjecture for uniform trees
record.statement:
Let $r\ge 2$, let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be $r$-uniform trees of order $m$, and let $K_n^{(r)}$ be the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. **The Ramsey equivalence conjecture for uniform trees.**

$$
R(T_1,K_n^{(r)};r)=R(T_2,K_n^{(r)};r).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the Ramsey number against a complete $r$-uniform hypergraph depends only on the order of the $r$-uniform tree, not on its structure. It is presented as one of several conjectures arising from the work, with no resolution supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Mark Budden and Andrew Penland, “Trees and n-Good Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1710.05731 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05731

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

record.title: Gruslys, Leader and Tan's hypercube edge-packing conjecture
record.statement:
Let $Q_k$ denote the $k$-dimensional hypercube, and let $H$ be a non-empty subgraph of $Q_k$. An **edge-packing by $H$** is a collection of edge-disjoint copies of $H$.

**Gruslys, Leader and Tan's conjecture.** For $kge 1$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that the edges of $Q_n$ can be covered by edge-disjoint copies of $H$; the copies of $H$ are not required to be induced.

This is an edge-packing analogue of the vertex-packing results for hypercubes. The supplied text gives no resolution status for this conjecture.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Natasha Morrison and Alex Scott, “Partitioning the vertices of a torus into isomorphic subgraphs”, arXiv:1710.07255 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07255

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2017). “However, in general Conjecture is false.”

record.title: Non-degeneracy conjecture for Riemannian Schwarzschild–anti de Sitter metrics
record.statement:
Let $P_L$ be the linearisation, at Riemannian Kottler metrics with negative cosmological constant, of the $TT$-gauge-fixed Einstein operator. Let $K
ull$ denote the curvature parameter and let $\mu$ be the mass parameter. In spacetime dimension $n+2=4$, the exceptional value is

$$
\mu=\frac{n}{n+1}\left(\ell\sqrt{\frac{n-1}{n+1}}\right)^{n-1}.
$$

**Non-degeneracy conjecture.** $P_L$ has no $L^2$-kernel except if $K=1$ and $\mu$ is given by the exceptional value above.

This conjecture proposes that the numerical and analytical non-degeneracy results for Riemannian Kottler metrics extend to all topologies and spacetime dimensions, apart from the exceptional spherical mass value.
record.source_name: Piotr T. Chruściel, Erwann Delay and Paul Klinger, “On non-degeneracy of Riemannian Schwarzschild-anti de Sitter metrics”, arXiv:1710.07597 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07597

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

record.title: The complete-uniform-hypergraph host conjecture
record.statement:
Let $r,t,n$ be positive integers, and let $K_n^{(r)}$ be the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices, with $K_t^{(r)}$ defined analogously. Write $_{K_t^{(r)}}(k)$ and $_{K_t^{(r)}}^*(k)$ for the simple-host and multigraph-host extremal functions.

**Complete-host conjecture.** If

$$
k=(K_n^{(r)},K_t^{(r)})+1,
$$

then

$$
_{K_t^{(r)}}(k)=_{K_t^{(r)}}^*(k)={n\choose r},
$$

and the unique extremal graph is $K_n^{(r)}$.
This conjecture extends the exact complete-host result beyond the values of $k$ immediately above the complete-hypergraph Turán number; the statement does not specify a resolution.
record.source_name: Joseph Briggs and Christopher Cox, “Inverting the Turán Problem”, arXiv:1711.02082 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.02082

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

record.title: The characterization of P-positions for triangular chocolate bar games when k is 1 modulo 4
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $(x,y,z)$ denote a position in the triangular chocolate bar game, with $x,y,z\in Z_{\geq 0}$. A position is a **P-position** if the next player has no winning strategy, and write $\oplus$ for bitwise exclusive OR. **P-position characterization.** When $k=4m+1$ for some $m\in Z_{\geq 0}$, $(x,y,z)$ is a P-position if and only if

$$
(x-1)\oplus y\oplus (z-1)=0.
$$

The statement is supported in the paper by computational evidence from CGSuite for the case $k=5$; its status is not established by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ryohei Miyadera, Shunsuke Nakamura and Masanori Fukui, “Impartial Triangular Chocolate Bar Games”, arXiv:1711.04954 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.04954

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

record.title: Guggiari's path-cover conjecture for 2-edge-coloured complete symmetric digraphs
record.statement: Let $\vec{K}_{\mathbb{N}}$ be the complete symmetric digraph on the positive integers, and let a **2-edge-colouring** assign one of two colours, red or blue, to every directed edge. A directed path is a finite or one-way infinite sequence of distinct vertices in which each consecutive pair is joined by a directed edge in the forward direction. Fix $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$. **Guggiari's conjecture.** If the colouring contains no red directed path of length $\ell$, then the vertices of $\vec{K}_{\mathbb{N}}$ can be covered by at most $\ell$ vertex-disjoint blue directed paths. This would give a sharp path-cover consequence of forbidding a red directed path of prescribed length; the supplied text attributes the conjecture to Guggiari but gives no resolution status, so it remains open here.
record.source_name: Carl Bürger and Max Pitz, “Decomposing edge-coloured complete symmetric digraphs into monochromatic paths”, arXiv:1711.08711 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.08711

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

record.title: Conjecture on lifting spectral numbers to spectral pairs
record.statement: Let $S$ be a matrix in a Seifert form stratum of $T(n,\mathbb R)$ that is not met by $\bigcup_{k=1,2}T_{{\rm HOR}k}(n,\mathbb R)$. Let $\operatorname{Sp}(S)$ and $\operatorname{Spp}(S)$ denote its spectral numbers and spectral pairs. **Lifting conjecture.** The spectral numbers $\operatorname{Sp}(S)$ lift in a natural way to the spectral pairs $\operatorname{Spp}(S)$. The claim would provide spectral-pair data for Seifert form strata not reached by the HOR-matrix families. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Sven Balnojan and Claus Hertling, “Conjectures on spectral numbers for upper triangular matrices and for singularities”, arXiv:1712.00388 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.00388

record.title: Johnson's conjecture on realizability of critical points
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda=\{\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n\}\subset\mathbb{C}$ with $n\ge 2$ be a list, let

$$
p(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(z-\lambda_i),
$$

and let $\Lambda'=\{\mu_1,\dots,\mu_{n-1}\}$ be the list of zeros of $p'$. A list is **realizable** if it is the spectrum of an entrywise nonnegative matrix. **Johnson's conjecture.** If $\Lambda$ is realizable, then $\Lambda'$ is realizable. This conjecture asks whether realizability is inherited by the list of critical points of the polynomial whose roots form a realizable list. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Sarah L Hoover, Daniel A. McCormick, Pietro Paparella and Amber R. Thrall, “On the realizability of the critical points of a realizable list”, arXiv:1712.05454 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.05454

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: Resistance increment conjecture for straight linear k-trees
record.statement:
Let $G$ be the straight linear $k$-tree with $k\geq 1$ and $n$ vertices, and let $H$ be the straight linear $k$-tree with $n+1$ vertices. Let $r_G$ and $r_H$ denote resistance distance in these graphs. **Resistance increment conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\bigl(r_H(1,n+1)-r_G(1,n)\bigr)=\frac{6}{k(k+1)(2k+1)}.
$$

For $k=2$, the paper proves the corresponding increment is $1/5$ and hence the end-to-end resistance is unbounded. The formula for general $k$ is supported by empirical evidence and remains open.
record.source_name: Wayne Barrett, Emily J. Evans and Amanda E. Francis, “Resistance distance in straight linear 2-trees”, arXiv:1712.05883 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.05883

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: Hochstättler's perfect-matching formulation for cubic digraphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a 3-edge-connected, cubic digraph. A **perfect matching without a directed cut** is a perfect matching that contains no directed edge-cut. **Hochstättler's equivalent conjecture.** $G$ contains a perfect matching without a directed cut. This is presented as an equivalent reformulation of Hochstättler's conjecture, and the source's diagram classifies the corresponding upper conjectures as false.
record.source_name: Kolja Knauer and Petru Valicov, “Cuts in matchings of 3-connected cubic graphs”, arXiv:1712.06143 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.06143

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Characterization of finite pairs of chi-unavoidable connected ordered graphs
record.statement: Let $H$ and $H'$ be $chi$-unavoidable connected ordered graphs, each with at least two edges. **Connected ordered-graph finiteness conjecture.** The pair $(H,H')$ is Ramsey finite if and only if $(H,H')$ is either a pair consisting of a right star and an almost increasing right caterpillar, or a pair consisting of a left star and an almost increasing left caterpillar. The conjecture concerns the remaining connected $chi$-unavoidable cases identified in the paper; the source reports a proof of one small case in a dissertation but leaves the general characterization open.
record.source_name: Jonathan Rollin, “Minimal Ordered Ramsey Graphs”, arXiv:1712.09034 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09034

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2017). “In the ordered setting several cases remain open, even if Conjectures and hold.”

record.title: Function-field Freiman conjecture for spaces of small combinatorial genus
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field and let $F$ be an extension field of $K$. Let $S$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-subspace of $F$ such that $K\subset S$. Define the **combinatorial genus** $\gamma$ of $S$ by

$$
\dim S^2=2\dim S-1+\gamma.
$$

Assume that $\gamma\leqslant\dim S-3$. **Function-field Freiman conjecture.** If $g$ is the genus of the field $K(S)$, then

$$
g\leqslant\gamma,
$$

and there exists a Riemann–Roch space $L(D)$ containing $S$ such that

$$
\dim L(D)\leqslant\dim S+\gamma-g.
$$

This is a function-field analogue of Freiman-type structure results: spaces with small product growth should be controlled by Riemann–Roch spaces on curves of genus bounded by their combinatorial genus. The source presents the assertion as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Christine Bachoc, Alain Couvreur and Gilles Zémor, “Towards a function field version of Freiman's Theorem”, arXiv:1709.00087 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.00087

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2017).
